objects.description: Enumeration for MAT file access modes (read-only or read/write).
Enumeration of MAT file format versions.

objects.definition:
enum matio_types
{
    MAT_T_UNKNOWN = 0,
    MAT_T_INT8 = 1,
    MAT_T_UINT8 = 2,
    MAT_T_INT16 = 3,
    MAT_T_UINT16 = 4,
    MAT_T_INT32 = 5,
    MAT_T_UINT32 = 6,
    MAT_T_SINGLE = 7,
    MAT_T_DOUBLE = 9,
    MAT_T_INT64 = 12,
    MAT_T_UINT64 = 13,
    MAT_T_MATRIX = 14,
    MAT_T_COMPRESSED = 15,
    MAT_T_UTF8 = 16,
    MAT_T_UTF16 = 17,
    MAT_T_UTF32 = 18,

    MAT_T_STRING = 20,
    MAT_T_CELL = 21,
    MAT_T_STRUCT = 22,
    MAT_T_ARRAY = 23,
    MAT_T_FUNCTION = 24
};
objects.description: Enumeration of MATLAB data (storage) types used by matio.

objects.definition:
enum matio_classes
{
    MAT_C_EMPTY = 0,
    MAT_C_CELL = 1,
    MAT_C_STRUCT = 2,
    MAT_C_OBJECT = 3,
    MAT_C_CHAR = 4,
    MAT_C_SPARSE = 5,
    MAT_C_DOUBLE = 6,
    MAT_C_SINGLE = 7,
    MAT_C_INT8 = 8,
    MAT_C_UINT8 = 9,
    MAT_C_INT16 = 10,
    MAT_C_UINT16 = 11,
    MAT_C_INT32 = 12,
    MAT_C_UINT32 = 13,
    MAT_C_INT64 = 14,
    MAT_C_UINT64 = 15,
    MAT_C_FUNCTION = 16,
    MAT_C_OPAQUE = 17
};
objects.description: Enumeration of MATLAB array classes.
Bitmask flags for array properties and allocation behavior.
Enumeration for per-variable compression options (v5 files).
Enumeration controlling how variables are looked up (by name or index).
Split-storage complex number holding separate real and imaginary data pointers. The pointed-to buffers must match the element type of the owning variable.
Opaque handle to an open MAT file. The structure is intentionally incomplete here; managed via the matio API.
Incomplete (private) per-variable internal data owned by matvar_t. Not user-accessible.
Represents a MATLAB variable, including metadata (name, class, type, flags), dimensions, data pointer, and implementation-private state.
Sparse matrix storage describing compressed column format arrays (ir, jc) and associated data buffer. nzmax bounds nonzero capacity; ndata is number of stored (real or complex) values.
Function pointer type for iteration predicates used to filter variables during sequential reads. Return 1 to read, 0 to skip.
Public typedef for a 64-bit signed integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically int64_t).
Public typedef for a 64-bit unsigned integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically uint64_t).
Public typedef for a 32-bit signed integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically int32_t).
Public typedef for a 32-bit unsigned integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically uint32_t).
Public typedef for a 16-bit signed integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically int16_t).
Public typedef for a 16-bit unsigned integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically uint16_t).
Public typedef for an 8-bit signed integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically int8_t).
Public typedef for an 8-bit unsigned integer. Underlying base type is platform-provided (typically uint8_t).

functions.name: Mat_GetLibraryVersion
functions.description: Retrieves the matio library version numbers (major, minor, release). Call to detect the runtime library version.
requirements: major, minor, and release must be non-NULL pointers where results will be stored.

functions.name: Mat_SetVerbose
functions.description: Configures library verbosity. Likely sets a verbosity level and/or output stream/severity mask.
requirements: verb is an integer verbosity level; accepted range/semantics are unspecified (unknown).
s is an additional selector/flag for verbosity output; semantics unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_SetDebug
functions.description: Enables or configures debug logging level for the library.
requirements: d is an integer debug level; accepted range/semantics are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_Critical
functions.description: Logs a critical error message using printf-style formatting. Intended for error reporting without terminating the process.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_Error
functions.description: Reports a fatal error using printf-style formatting and does not return (terminates the program or long-jumps). Use for unrecoverable errors only.
requirements: This function does not return; callers must not rely on control flow continuing after the call.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_Help
functions.description: Displays help/usage text and does not return (terminates the program).
requirements: This function does not return; callers must not rely on control flow continuing after the call.
helpstr must be a valid NULL-terminated array of C strings (unknown exact termination requirements; typically last pointer is NULL).

functions.name: Mat_LogInit
functions.description: Initializes the library’s logging subsystem, optionally tagging messages with the program name.
requirements: prog_name should be a valid, null-terminated string or NULL if unsupported (exact handling of NULL unknown).
Must be called before other logging functions to ensure initialization (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_LogClose
functions.description: Shuts down the library’s logging subsystem and releases related resources.
requirements: Should be called after Mat_LogInit and when logging is no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_LogInitFunc
functions.signature: int Mat_LogInitFunc(const char *prog_name, void (*log_func)(int log_level, const char *message));
functions.description: Initializes logging with a user-provided callback that receives log messages and levels.
requirements: log_func must be a valid function pointer that safely handles callbacks from the library.
prog_name should be a valid, null-terminated string or NULL if unsupported (exact handling unknown).
Should be called before emitting log messages (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_Message
functions.description: Emits an informational/message-level log using printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_DebugMessage
functions.description: Emits a debug-level log message using printf-style formatting and a specified debug level.
requirements: level selects the debug severity; accepted range/semantics are unspecified (unknown).
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_VerbMessage
functions.description: Emits a verbosity-controlled log message using printf-style formatting and the given level.
requirements: level selects the verbosity; accepted range/semantics are unspecified (unknown).
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_Warning
functions.description: Logs a warning message using printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.

functions.name: Mat_SizeOf
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scalar element of the specified MAT data type (MAT_T_*).
requirements: data_type must be a valid enum matio_types value; behavior for MAT_T_UNKNOWN or unsupported types is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_SizeOfClass
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes per element for a given MATLAB class (MAT_C_*).
requirements: class_type should be a valid MAT_C_* value; behavior for invalid values is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_CreateVer
functions.signature: mat_t *Mat_CreateVer(const char *matname, const char *hdr_str, enum mat_ft mat_file_ver);
functions.description: Creates a new MAT file with the given filename, header text, and file version (e.g., MAT_FT_MAT5, MAT_FT_MAT73). Returns a handle on success.
requirements: matname must be a valid filesystem path to a file to create; the process must have write permissions.
hdr_str should be a valid header string or NULL if default header is desired (exact behavior for NULL unknown).
mat_file_ver must be one of enum mat_ft (MAT_FT_MAT5, MAT_FT_MAT73, MAT_FT_MAT4).
Caller must close the returned mat_t* with Mat_Close when done.

functions.name: Mat_Close
functions.description: Closes an open MAT file and releases associated resources.
requirements: mat must be a valid mat_t* previously returned by Mat_Open or Mat_CreateVer.
Do not use mat after this call.

functions.name: Mat_Open
functions.description: Opens an existing MAT file with the given access mode (MAT_ACC_RDONLY or MAT_ACC_RDWR). Returns a file handle on success.
requirements: matname must be a valid path to an existing file.
mode must be a valid mat_acc value (MAT_ACC_RDONLY or MAT_ACC_RDWR).
Caller must close the returned mat_t* with Mat_Close when done.

functions.name: Mat_GetFileAccessMode
functions.description: Returns the access mode (read-only or read/write) with which the MAT file was opened.
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.

functions.name: Mat_GetFilename
functions.description: Returns the filename associated with the MAT file handle.
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.
Returned pointer remains valid while mat is valid; do not free (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_GetHeader
functions.description: Returns the header string stored in the MAT file (e.g., descriptive text).
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_GetVersion
functions.description: Returns the MAT file format version of the open file (MAT_FT_*).
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.

functions.name: Mat_GetDir
functions.description: Returns an array of variable names in the MAT file and stores the count in n.
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.
n must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of names.
The returned array and strings are owned by the library; lifetime and freeing rules are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_Rewind
functions.description: Resets reading position to the beginning of the MAT file (for sequential iteration over variables).
requirements: mat must be a valid pointer to an open MAT file.

functions.name: Mat_VarCalloc
functions.description: Allocates and returns a zero-initialized matvar_t structure.
requirements: Caller must free the returned object with Mat_VarFree when done.

functions.name: Mat_VarCreate
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarCreate(const char *name, enum matio_classes class_type, enum matio_types data_type, int rank, const size_t *dims, const void *data, int opt);
functions.description: Creates a matvar_t describing a MATLAB variable with the given name, class, data type, dimensions, and optional initial data. opt modifies behavior (e.g., MAT_F_DONT_COPY_DATA).
requirements: name should be a valid null-terminated string (may be NULL for anonymous variables; exact behavior unknown).
class_type must be a valid MAT_C_* value.
data_type must be a valid MAT_T_* value consistent with class_type.
rank must be >= 0; if >0, dims must point to an array of length rank.
dims entries must be >0 to represent valid extents (exact allowance for zero unknown).
If data is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer large enough for product(dims) elements of data_type.
opt may include MAT_F_DONT_COPY_DATA to indicate ownership remains with caller (inferred).
Caller must free the returned object with Mat_VarFree when done or write with Mat_VarWrite.

functions.name: Mat_VarCreateStruct
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarCreateStruct(const char *name, int rank, const size_t *dims, const char **fields, unsigned nfields);
functions.description: Creates a MATLAB struct variable with specified dimensions and field names.
requirements: name should be a valid null-terminated string (exact NULL handling unknown).
rank must be >= 0; if >0, dims must point to an array of length rank.
fields may be NULL if nfields==0; otherwise must contain nfields valid field-name strings.
Caller must free the returned object with Mat_VarFree when done.

functions.name: Mat_VarDelete
functions.description: Deletes a variable by name from a writable MAT file.
requirements: mat must be opened in a mode that allows modifications (likely MAT_ACC_RDWR).
name must be a valid variable name present in the file (behavior if missing unspecified).

functions.name: Mat_VarDuplicate
functions.description: Creates a duplicate of a matvar_t, possibly controlling deep/shallow copy via opt.
requirements: in must point to a valid matvar_t.
opt controls duplication semantics; exact flags unspecified (unknown).
Caller must free the returned object with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarFree
functions.description: Frees a matvar_t and any associated resources allocated by the library.
requirements: matvar may be NULL (behavior unspecified; typically a no-op).
After freeing, the pointer must not be used.

functions.name: Mat_VarGetCell
functions.description: Returns the cell element at the linear index from a cell array variable.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_CELL variable.
index must be within the valid linear range [0, numel).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetCells
functions.signature: matvar_t **Mat_VarGetCells(const matvar_t *matvar, const int *start, const int *stride, const int *edge);
functions.description: Returns a block of cell elements defined by start/stride/edge over each dimension.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_CELL variable.
start, stride, and edge must each point to arrays of length matvar->rank.
All requested indices must be within bounds: start[d] >= 0, edge[d] >= 0, and start[d] + (edge[d]-1)*stride[d] < dims[d] (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetCellsLinear
functions.signature: matvar_t **Mat_VarGetCellsLinear(const matvar_t *matvar, int start, int stride, int edge);
functions.description: Returns a linearly strided subset of cell elements.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_CELL variable.
start >= 0, edge >= 0, and start + (edge-1)*stride must be within the total number of elements (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetSize
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the variable’s data payload.
requirements: matvar must be a valid pointer to a matvar_t.

functions.name: Mat_VarGetNumberOfFields
functions.description: Returns the number of fields in a struct variable.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.

functions.name: Mat_VarAddStructField
functions.description: Adds a new field to a struct variable’s field list.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable that permits modification.
fieldname must be a valid, null-terminated field name string.

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructFieldnames
functions.description: Returns an array of field name strings for a struct variable.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
The returned array and strings are owned by the library; freeing rules are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructFieldByIndex
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarGetStructFieldByIndex(const matvar_t *matvar, size_t field_index, size_t index);
functions.description: Retrieves a struct field’s value by its field index and element index.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
field_index must be less than the number of fields.
index must be within the number of struct elements (linear index).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructFieldByName
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarGetStructFieldByName(const matvar_t *matvar, const char *field_name, size_t index);
functions.description: Retrieves a struct field’s value by field name and element index.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
field_name must be a valid, null-terminated string.
index must be within the number of struct elements (linear index).

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructField
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarGetStructField(const matvar_t *matvar, void *name_or_index, int opt, int index);
functions.description: Generic struct field accessor by either name or index depending on opt (MAT_BY_NAME or MAT_BY_INDEX).
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
opt must be MAT_BY_NAME or MAT_BY_INDEX (enum matio_lookup).
If opt==MAT_BY_NAME, name_or_index must point to a C string; if MAT_BY_INDEX, it must point to an integer index value (exact type of pointed integer is unspecified in this header; unknown).
index must be within the linear range of struct elements.

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructs
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarGetStructs(const matvar_t *matvar, const int *start, const int *stride, const int *edge, int copy_fields);
functions.description: Extracts a subarray of a struct variable as a new matvar_t, optionally copying field lists.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
start, stride, and edge must each point to arrays of length matvar->rank.
All requested indices must be within bounds (inferred).
copy_fields controls duplication of field metadata; semantics unspecified (unknown).
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarGetStructsLinear
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarGetStructsLinear(const matvar_t *matvar, int start, int stride, int edge, int copy_fields);
functions.description: Extracts a linearly strided subset of a struct variable as a new matvar_t.
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
start >= 0, edge >= 0, and start + (edge-1)*stride must be within the number of elements (inferred).
copy_fields controls duplication of field metadata; semantics unspecified (unknown).
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarPrint
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of a matvar_t, optionally including data contents.
requirements: matvar must be a valid pointer to a matvar_t.
printdata controls whether to print data; nonzero to print, zero for metadata only (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_VarRead
functions.description: Reads a variable by name from an open MAT file and returns a newly allocated matvar_t with data.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
name must be a valid, null-terminated variable name string.
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadData
functions.signature: int Mat_VarReadData(mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, void *data, const int *start, const int *stride, const int *edge);
functions.description: Reads a hyperslab of a variable’s data into a user-provided buffer using start/stride/edge per dimension.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
matvar must describe the target variable in the file (from ReadInfo or similar).
data must point to a buffer large enough to hold the requested elements in the variable’s data_type.
start, stride, and edge must each be arrays of length matvar->rank, within bounds (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_VarReadDataAll
functions.description: Reads all data for the specified variable described by matvar into memory managed by matvar.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
matvar must be a valid variable info; on success matvar->data will be populated.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadDataLinear
functions.signature: int Mat_VarReadDataLinear(mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, void *data, int start, int stride, int edge);
functions.description: Reads a linearly strided subset of the variable’s data into a user buffer.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
matvar must describe the variable.
data must point to a buffer large enough for the requested elements.
start >= 0, edge >= 0, and range must be within total elements (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_VarReadInfo
functions.description: Reads only metadata (shape, type, etc.) for a variable by name without loading its data.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
name must be a valid, null-terminated variable name string.
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadNext
functions.description: Sequentially reads the next variable (metadata and data) from the MAT file.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading and positioned appropriately (use Mat_Rewind to restart).
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadNextPredicate
functions.description: Iterates variables, returning the next one for which pred(name, user_data) returns 1 (reads data).
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
pred must be a valid callback function; it will be called with each variable name.
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadNextInfo
functions.description: Sequentially reads only metadata for the next variable from the MAT file.
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarReadNextInfoPredicate
functions.description: Iterates variables, returning the next one for which pred(name, user_data) returns 1 (metadata only).
requirements: mat must be a valid MAT file opened for reading.
pred must be a valid callback function.
Caller must free the returned matvar_t with Mat_VarFree.

functions.name: Mat_VarSetCell
functions.description: Sets a cell array element at linear index to the provided cell value, returning the previous cell (or possibly the set cell).
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_CELL variable.
index must be within the valid linear range.
cell must be a valid matvar_t or NULL to clear (exact semantics unknown).
Ownership/lifetime transfer semantics are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_VarSetStructFieldByIndex
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarSetStructFieldByIndex(matvar_t *matvar, size_t field_index, size_t index, matvar_t *field);
functions.description: Sets a struct field at field_index for the struct element at index, returning any previous field value (if applicable).
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
field_index must be less than the number of fields.
index must be within the number of struct elements.
field must be a valid matvar_t or NULL (exact behavior unknown).
Ownership/lifetime transfer semantics are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_VarSetStructFieldByName
functions.signature: matvar_t *Mat_VarSetStructFieldByName(matvar_t *matvar, const char *field_name, size_t index, matvar_t *field);
functions.description: Sets a struct field by name for the struct element at index, returning any previous field value (if applicable).
requirements: matvar must be a valid MAT_C_STRUCT variable.
field_name must be a valid, null-terminated field name.
index must be within the number of struct elements.
field must be a valid matvar_t or NULL (exact behavior unknown).
Ownership/lifetime transfer semantics are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: Mat_VarWrite
functions.signature: int Mat_VarWrite(mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, enum matio_compression compress);
functions.description: Writes a complete variable (metadata and data) to an open MAT file, optionally with compression (MAT version 5 only).
requirements: mat must be opened with write permissions (MAT_ACC_RDWR).
matvar must be a valid, fully described variable (dims, type, data when applicable).
compress must be MAT_COMPRESSION_NONE or MAT_COMPRESSION_ZLIB; compression only applies to MAT5 files.

functions.name: Mat_VarWriteAppend
functions.signature: int Mat_VarWriteAppend(mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, enum matio_compression compress, int dim);
functions.description: Appends data to an existing variable along a specified dimension, optionally with compression.
requirements: mat must be opened with write permissions (MAT_ACC_RDWR).
matvar must describe the variable and appended data layout correctly; dimensions must be compatible (inferred).
dim selects the dimension along which to append; must be a valid dimension index.
compress must be MAT_COMPRESSION_NONE or MAT_COMPRESSION_ZLIB (MAT5 only).

functions.name: Mat_VarWriteInfo
functions.description: Writes only the variable’s metadata (header) to the MAT file, preparing to write data later.
requirements: mat must be an open MAT file with write permissions (despite const qualifier, it refers to a writable handle).
matvar must be a valid variable description.

functions.name: Mat_VarWriteData
functions.signature: int Mat_VarWriteData(const mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, void *data, const int *start, const int *stride, const int *edge);
functions.description: Writes a hyperslab of raw data to a variable previously defined with Mat_VarWriteInfo, using start/stride/edge indexing.
requirements: mat must be an open MAT file with write permissions.
matvar must correspond to a variable header already written or to be written; layout must match.
data must point to a buffer with at least the number of elements indicated by edge and data_type.
start, stride, and edge must each be arrays of length matvar->rank and within bounds (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_CalcSingleSubscript
functions.signature: int Mat_CalcSingleSubscript(int rank, const int *dims, const int *subs);
functions.description: Computes a linear index from multi-dimensional subscripts given integer dims and subs arrays.
requirements: rank must be >= 0.
dims must point to an array of length rank with positive extents.
subs must point to an array of length rank with 0 <= subs[d] < dims[d] (inferred).

functions.name: Mat_CalcSingleSubscript2
functions.signature: int Mat_CalcSingleSubscript2(int rank, const size_t *dims, const size_t *subs, size_t *index);
functions.description: Computes a linear index from multi-dimensional subscripts (size_t-based) and stores it in index.
requirements: rank must be >= 0.
dims and subs must each point to arrays of length rank; for all d, 0 <= subs[d] < dims[d] (inferred).
index must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.

functions.name: Mat_CalcSubscripts
functions.signature: int *Mat_CalcSubscripts(int rank, const int *dims, int index);
functions.description: Converts a linear index into multi-dimensional subscripts given dims, returning a newly allocated array of length rank.
requirements: rank must be >= 0.
dims must point to an array of length rank with positive extents.
index must be within the valid linear range [0, product(dims)).
Caller must free the returned array with the appropriate deallocator (free), unless library manages it (ownership unspecified; unknown).

functions.name: Mat_CalcSubscripts2
functions.signature: size_t *Mat_CalcSubscripts2(int rank, const size_t *dims, size_t index);
functions.description: Converts a linear index into multi-dimensional subscripts (size_t-based), returning a newly allocated array of length rank.
requirements: rank must be >= 0.
dims must point to an array of length rank with positive extents.
index must be within [0, product(dims)).
Caller must free the returned array with the appropriate deallocator (ownership unspecified; unknown).

functions.name: Mat_Create
functions.description: Creates a new MATLAB MAT file using the library’s default file format. Mat_Create is a function-like macro that expands to Mat_CreateVer(matname, hdr_str, MAT_FT_DEFAULT). The default format (MAT_FT_DEFAULT) is MAT_FT_MAT5 per the public configuration. Typical usage: call Mat_Create with the output filename and an optional/desired header string; on success it returns a mat_t* handle that should later be closed with Mat_Close.
requirements: This is a macro alias for Mat_CreateVer(matname, hdr_str, MAT_FT_DEFAULT); ensure matio.h is included so the macro is visible.
matname should be a valid NUL-terminated path string to the file to create (inferred from parameter name and usage).
hdr_str should be a NUL-terminated string for the MAT-file header text (inferred from parameter name and usage).
Check the return value: on failure it may return NULL; callers must handle this (inferred from library patterns and return type).
On success, the returned mat_t* must be released by calling Mat_Close to avoid resource leaks (inferred from presence of Mat_Close(mat_t *)).
The created file will use the default format MAT_FT_MAT5 as defined by MAT_FT_DEFAULT in matio_pubconf.h.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target datatype: printf-style format string inputs used indirectly via FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# The fuzzer stubs call logging functions with fixed format strings and pass FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# as a %s argument. Therefore, interesting valid inputs are arbitrary strings that may contain:
# - Plain ASCII text (short/long, with/without spaces)
# - Edge characters (NUL not allowed inside; buffer will be used as C-string up to first NUL)
# - Embedded percent signs that are safe as literal text when used as the %s argument
#   (since they are part of the string data, not the format string). We should escape them
#   by doubling (%%) to avoid accidental interpretation in places where a user might reuse the
#   string as a format later. However, here the %s is data, so single % is fine for validity.
# - Newlines, tabs, and other whitespace to exercise message handling.
# - UTF-8 multibyte sequences to exercise logging code paths that handle non-ASCII.
# - Varied lengths but <= 4096 bytes.
# We will generate a bytes buffer that could seed the fuzzing engine to supply FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and related calls. Since multiple stubs only use %s and an integer computed from random,
# any string content is valid. We aim to cover diverse content deterministically per seed.

MAX_LEN = 1024  # keep under 4096 comfortably

ASCII_PRINT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "αβγδεζηθ",   # Greek
    "Привет",      # Cyrillic
    "こんにちは",   # Japanese Hiragana
    "مرحبا",       # Arabic
    "🙂🙃😉🥳",       # Emoji
    "𝟘𝟙𝟚𝟛𝟜𝟝",      # Math bold digits
    "ñáéíóúü",     # Latin-1 accents
]

PERCENT_PATTERNS = [
    "%", "%%", "%d", "%s", "%x", "%#x", "%08x", "%ld", "%lld",
    "%.2f", "%g", "%p", "%zu", "%jd"
]

CONTROL_SETS = [
    "\n", "\r\n", "\t", "\v", "\f", "\0",  # note: embedded NUL (\0) terminates in C, but
    # as bytes we can include it; however, providing NUL could truncate the message early, still valid.
]

PREFIXES = [
    "", "INFO:", "WARN:", "DEBUG:", "CRIT:", "[module]", "{json}", "path:",
]

SUFFIXES = [
    "", " end", "!", "?", " #tag", " [ok]", " [fail]", " ::done",
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(r.choice(ASCII_PRINT) for _ in range(n))


def _chunky_string(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Start with a prefix to simulate log categories
    parts.append(r.choice(PREFIXES))
    # Compose with random mix of ascii, percent patterns, utf8 snippets, and controls
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        choice = r.randrange(6)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(1, 32)))
        elif choice == 1:
            # insert percent patterns separated by spaces to avoid accidental contiguous sequences
            pat = r.choice(PERCENT_PATTERNS)
            parts.append(pat)
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(r.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS))
        elif choice == 3:
            parts.append(r.choice(CONTROL_SETS))
        elif choice == 4:
            parts.append(" ")
        else:
            # small numbers / words
            parts.append(str(r.randint(-999999, 999999)))
    parts.append(r.choice(SUFFIXES))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Trim to requested length, but avoid cutting in middle of a surrogate pair: Python uses UTF-32/UTF-16 internally,
    # but slicing by code point is safe; then encode to UTF-8.
    return s[:target_len]


def _build_message(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a target length with a bias toward small and some larger cases
    roll = r.random()
    if roll < 0.5:
        target = r.randint(0, 64)
    elif roll < 0.85:
        target = r.randint(65, 256)
    else:
        target = r.randint(257, min(1024, MAX_LEN))

    s = _chunky_string(r, target)

    # Optionally wrap with brackets/time-like patterns
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        s = f"[{r.randint(0,23):02d}:{r.randint(0,59):02d}:{r.randint(0,59):02d}] " + s
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s = s + f" (code={r.randint(0,9999)})"

    # Ensure it is a valid UTF-8 byte sequence
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')

    # Optionally inject a NUL to test truncation behavior; safe for C strings though it truncates later content
    if len(b) > 0 and r.random() < 0.15:
        pos = r.randint(0, min(len(b), 64))  # early NULs more interesting
        b = b[:pos] + b"\x00" + b[pos:]

    # Guarantee not exceeding 4096
    return b[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_message(r)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for inputs targeting matio logging and file-creation fuzzers.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects a NUL-terminated string used as payload/header text.
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME expects a valid-looking filesystem path string.
# The fuzzer harness will pick among these buffers; we just return one buffer.
# We embed multiple NUL-terminated strings concatenated, so the harness can
# consume them sequentially if it slices from the buffer.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:/\\[]{}()+=%@#~!$^&'`"

def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _header_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Common MAT header-like strings are 116 bytes in MAT v5, but any text is accepted by API.
    # Provide diverse, valid UTF-8 messages without NULs; fuzzer will append NUL terminator.
    base = [
        "MATLAB 5.0 MAT-file, Platform: GLNXA64, Created on: 01-Jan-2025 00:00:00",
        "MATLAB 7.3 MAT-file (HDF5)",
        "Test Header — unicode ✓",
        "",
        _rand_printable(r, 5, 80),
    ]
    # Ensure variety of lengths including long header but keep under limits
    long_text = ("Header:" + _rand_printable(r, 50, 200))[:240]
    base.append(long_text)
    return [s.encode('utf-8') for s in base]

def _filename_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Create plausible paths; the harness will attempt to create files, so avoid absolute forbidden paths.
    names = [
        "fuzz.mat",
        "out.mat",
        f"test_{r.randint(0,9999)}.mat",
        f"data_{_rand_printable(r,3,8)}.mat",
        f"subdir{subdir_sep(r)}file_{r.randint(1,100)}.mat",
        f"deep{subdir_sep(r)}nest{subdir_sep(r)}case_{_rand_printable(r,2,6)}.mat",
    ]
    # Include different extensions; library will still create the file.
    names += [
        f"file_{r.randint(0,999)}.mat5",
        f"hdf_{r.randint(0,999)}.mat73",
    ]
    # Prepend relative indicators sometimes
    decorated = []
    for n in names:
        prefix = r.choice(["", "./", "../", ".\\", "..\\"])  # cross-platform variety as text
        decorated.append(prefix + n)
    return [s.encode('utf-8') for s in decorated]

def subdir_sep(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(["/", "/", "\\"])  # bias toward Unix style

def _log_message_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    msgs = [
        "hello",
        "quick brown fox",
        "Δ unicode message",
        _rand_printable(r, 0, 64),
        "edge-case: spaces    and\ttabs",
        "json:{\"k\":1}",
        "path:C:/tmp/test.mat",
        "path:/tmp/test.mat",
    ]
    return [s.encode('utf-8') for s in msgs]

def _pack_c_strings(blobs: List[bytes], r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Pack as consecutive NUL-terminated strings; deduplicate and shuffle for variety
    unique = []
    seen = set()
    for b in blobs:
        if b not in seen:
            seen.add(b)
            unique.append(b)
    r.shuffle(unique)
    out = bytearray()
    for b in unique:
        # Ensure no embedded NUL
        b2 = b.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        if len(out) + len(b2) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += b2 + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Place filename first so FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME can pick the beginning easily.
    parts.extend(_filename_variants(r))

    # Then headers for Mat_Create/Mat_CreateVer
    parts.extend(_header_variants(r))

    # Then general log message payloads for Mat_Message/Warning/Critical/etc.
    parts.extend(_log_message_variants(r))

    # Also append a few random-sized numeric-like strings to exercise %d alongside %s contexts
    nums = [str(r.randint(-100000, 100000)).encode('ascii') for _ in range(6)]
    parts.extend(nums)

    # Finally, add some mixed content strings
    mixed = [
        ("mix:" + _rand_printable(r, 1, 40)).encode('utf-8'),
        ("hdr:" + _rand_printable(r, 10, 60)).encode('utf-8'),
    ]
    parts.extend(mixed)

    return _pack_c_strings(parts, r)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a valid program name string (NUL-terminated when used as C string).
# The fuzzer harness will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain a std::string and pass c_str() to
# Mat_LogInit/Mat_LogInitFunc. We therefore aim to return a bytes buffer that the fuzzer
# can use as initial corpus input to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR with interesting, but valid, values.
#
# Goals:
# - Provide short printable ASCII names, names with dots, dashes, underscores, version suffixes.
# - Include Unicode (UTF-8) examples that remain valid strings.
# - Include edge cases: very short (1 char), relatively long (but < 4096), names resembling paths
#   (with/without separators), names with spaces, mixed case, and with/without extensions.
# - Avoid embedded NUL characters because std::string treats them as data but C strings stop at NUL;
#   provide clean NUL-terminated semantics when passed via c_str().
# - Ensure non-empty data.

ASCII_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_SYMBOLS = "-_.+"
SPACEY = " "

# A small set of curated interesting names
CURATED = [
    "app",
    "a",
    "main",
    "prog",
    "test",
    "fuzz",
    "matio",
    "matio-fuzz",
    "matio_test",
    "matio.debug",
    "MATIO",
    "my-app",
    "my_app",
    "prog-1.0",
    "prog_2025-12-14",
    "logger",
    "tool",
    "cli",
    "service",
    "daemon",
    "mat-reader",
    "mat-writer",
    "matio-fuzzer",
    "u_test",
    "run",
    "bin",
    "x",
    # With extensions
    "prog.exe",
    "prog.sh",
    "prog.py",
    "prog.out",
    # With spaces
    "my app",
    "test runner",
    "matio fuzz",
    # With path-ish content (still valid string for program name tagging)
    "./prog",
    "../prog",
    "/usr/bin/prog",
    "C:/Program Files/prog",
    # Unicode examples
    "прога",           # Cyrillic
    "程序",             # CJK
    "ツール",            # Katakana
    "δοκιμή",          # Greek
    "árvíztűrő-prog",  # Accents
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "αβγ",
    "niño",
    "über",
    "工具",
    "инструмент",
    "テスト",
    "試験",
    "测试",
    "🙂",
]

EXTENSIONS = ["", ".exe", ".sh", ".py", ".out", ".bin", ".dll", ".so"]
PREFIXES = ["", "./", "../", "/usr/bin/", "/opt/", "C:/", "C:/Program Files/"]
SEPARATORS = ["-", "_", ".", "+", " "]

MAX_LEN = 512  # keep comfortably below 4096


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = ASCII_CHARS + SAFE_SYMBOLS + SPACEY
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces sometimes
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).strip() or "app"
    return s


def _rand_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # A token resembling a program base name
    kind = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if kind == 0:
        return rng.choice(CURATED)
    elif kind == 1:
        base = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)))
        # Optional version suffix
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            base += rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + str(rng.randint(0, 20)) + ("." + str(rng.randint(0, 9)) if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
        return base
    elif kind == 2:
        return _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 16)
    elif kind == 3:
        return rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    else:
        # Mixed case with symbols
        parts = [
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6))),
            rng.choice(["app", "tool", "prog", "svc", "cli", "fuzz"]),
        ]
        return rng.choice(SEPARATORS).join(parts)


def _compose_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a plausible program name with optional prefix and extension
    prefix = rng.choice(PREFIXES) if rng.random() < 0.4 else ""
    base_parts: List[str] = []
    # 1 to 3 tokens joined by separators (but avoid creating empty strings)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        tok = _rand_token(rng)
        if tok:
            base_parts.append(tok)
    sep = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
    base = sep.join(base_parts) if base_parts else "app"
    # Maybe add extension (avoid if looks like path dir ending with slash)
    ext = rng.choice(EXTENSIONS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
    name = prefix + base + ext
    # Bound length
    if len(name.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_LEN:
        # Truncate base sensibly
        trimmed = base.encode('utf-8')[: MAX_LEN - len(prefix.encode('utf-8')) - len(ext.encode('utf-8'))]
        # ensure valid UTF-8 by decoding with ignore and fallback
        base = trimmed.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore') or "app"
        name = prefix + base + ext
    return name


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose mode: curated, composed, or random ascii
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.25:
        name = rng.choice(CURATED)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        name = _compose_name(rng)
    else:
        name = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64)

    # Ensure non-empty and stripped of embedded NULs to keep it a clean C string when used via c_str().
    name = name.replace("\x00", "")
    if not name:
        name = "app"

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; no explicit NUL required because std::string manages termination.
    data = name.encode('utf-8')
    # Keep under global cap
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Note: Avoid embedding literal NUL bytes in the source string (some harnesses reject it).
# We will construct NUL terminators at runtime using bytes([0]).

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."


def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 10) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    if s in (".", ".."):
        s = s + "_"
    return s


def _rand_rel_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_component(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 10)))
    base = _rand_component(rng, 3, 12)
    ext = rng.choice([".mat", ".MAT", ".bin", ".dat", ".tmp"]) if rng.random() < 0.9 else ""
    fname = f"{base}{ext}"
    parts.append(fname)
    path = "/".join(parts)
    prefix = rng.choice(["", "./", "../", "subdir/"])
    return prefix + path


def _mat_v5_header_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = "MATLAB 5.0 MAT-file, Platform: PythonGen, Created by fuzz harness; "
    notes = [
        "Little-Endian", "Big-Endian", "Experimental", "UnitTest", "CI",
        "Compression=ZLIB", "Compression=NONE", "UTF-8"
    ]
    add = rng.choice(notes)
    text = (base + add + "; RandomSeed=" + str(rng.randrange(1_000_000)))
    if len(text) > 116:
        text = text[:116]
    else:
        text = text.ljust(116)
    return text


def _mat_v73_header_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = "MATLAB 7.3 MAT-file; HDF5 based; Generated by fuzz harness; "
    extra = f"Build={rng.randint(1000,9999)}; Seed={rng.randint(0, 1<<31)}"
    s = prefix + extra
    return s[:200]


def _generic_header(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    words = [
        "analysis", "signal", "image", "sparse", "struct", "cell", "double",
        "single", "int32", "uint8", "complex", "logical", "global"
    ]
    k = rng.randint(3, min(7, len(words)))
    sel = rng.sample(words, k=k)
    s = "MAT file generated for " + ", ".join(sel)
    return s[:180]


def _extra_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    toks: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        toks.append(_rand_rel_path(rng))
    toks.extend([
        "%s %d %f",
        "var", "dataset", "A", "B1", "field_name", "myStruct", "cellArray",
    ])
    toks.extend([
        "Usage: program [options] file.mat",
        "-v --verbose  increase verbosity",
        "-h --help     show this help"
    ])
    return toks


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    filename = _rand_rel_path(rng)
    hdr_main = _mat_v5_header_like(rng) if rng.random() < 0.6 else _mat_v73_header_like(rng)
    hdr_alt1 = _mat_v73_header_like(rng)
    hdr_alt2 = _generic_header(rng)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    def add(s: str):
        parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
        parts.append(bytes([0]))  # NUL terminator constructed at runtime

    add(filename)
    add(hdr_main)
    add(hdr_alt1)
    add(hdr_alt2)

    for tok in _extra_tokens(rng):
        add(tok)

    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Ensure the final byte is a NUL after truncation
        buf = buf[:4095] + bytes([0])
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    # MATLAB-like identifier: start with letter or underscore, then letters/digits/underscore
    start_chars = string.ascii_letters + "_"
    other_chars = start_chars + string.digits
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(start_chars)
    s += "".join(rng.choices(other_chars, k=max(0, n - 1)))
    return s

def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 40) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Favor identifiers but occasionally include spaces and punctuation
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:+/[](){}"
    return "".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n)).strip() or "x"

def _choose(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _gen_struct_field_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    nfields = rng.randint(1, 3)
    names = set()
    out = []
    for _ in range(nfields):
        # Mix of MATLAB-like identifiers and generic printable names
        name = _rand_identifier(rng) if rng.random() < 0.8 else _rand_printable(rng)
        # Ensure non-empty and unique to improve coverage
        while name in names or not name:
            name = _rand_identifier(rng)
        names.add(name)
        out.append(name)
    return out

def _encode_cstring_list(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate NUL-terminated strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls slices
    return b"".join(s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00" for s in strings)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # We target identifier/name string usage in the stubs:
    # - Struct field names for Mat_VarCreateStruct, Mat_VarAddStructField
    # - Names used by Mat_VarGetStructFieldByName and Mat_VarGetStructField
    # - Variable names for Mat_VarDelete
    # The fuzzer pulls multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls; provide a sequence of
    # reasonable, non-empty C strings to exercise different branches (by-name/index).

    buf_parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Field names for initial struct creation (1..3 fields)
    fields = _gen_struct_field_names(rng)
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list(fields))

    # 2) Additional field name for Mat_VarAddStructField
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list([_rand_identifier(rng)]))

    # 3) Names for Mat_VarGetStructFieldByName (may or may not exist)
    # Include: an existing field, a near miss, and a generic name
    if fields:
        existing = _choose(rng, fields)
    else:
        existing = _rand_identifier(rng)
    near_miss = existing + ("_" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "1")
    generic = _rand_identifier(rng)
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list([existing, near_miss, generic]))

    # 4) Names for Mat_VarGetStructField with MAT_BY_NAME branch
    # Provide a mix of existing and new names
    mix = []
    mix.extend(fields[:])
    mix.append(_rand_identifier(rng))
    mix.append(_rand_printable(rng))
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list(mix))

    # 5) Name for Mat_VarSetStructFieldByName
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list([_choose(rng, fields) if fields and rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_identifier(rng)]))

    # 6) Variable names for Mat_VarDelete
    # Provide several plausible variable names
    varnames = [
        _rand_identifier(rng),
        "x",
        "data",
        _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 12),
    ]
    buf_parts.append(_encode_cstring_list(varnames))

    # Ensure total length <= 4096 bytes
    out = b"".join(buf_parts)
    return out[:4096]
